# gitmoap_group_outbound_rule (Resource)

A host, a domain and every name below it, or an address or a range; on the ports given, `443` when none are; for the services and repositories given, every one when none are. Or send `from_destination` — a destination from the list — and the rule is its suggested one, recording where it came from. The answer carries any warning: a rule naming a host where anyone can publish admits every tenant of it, and an address rule sends lookups outside the organization's network. A rule naming an internal address, a domain at a public suffix, a range wider than `/16` or `/48`, or a mail port is refused. With `dry_run=true` the answer is the rule as it would be, and nothing changes. Only a person who can manage the organization's outbound settings may (its owners, with the built-in roles).

The token needs `outbound:manage` and `outbound:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

# The api repository's pipelines may call Stripe's API.
resource "gitmoap_group_outbound_rule" "stripe" {
  group_id       = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
  kind           = "host"
  value          = "api.stripe.com"
  services       = ["pipelines"]
  repository_ids = [data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id]
  note           = "Payment integration tests"
}

# Every name under the company's own domain, from every service and repository, on HTTPS and on
# the internal registry's port.
resource "gitmoap_group_outbound_rule" "internal" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
  kind     = "domain"
  value    = "*.acme.example"
  ports    = [443, 5000]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The organization's top-level group

### Optional

- `from_destination` (String) A destination an organization's code reached, counted per service, kind, port and decision
- `kind` (String) What a rule names.
- `note` (String) Why an outbound rule exists, shown beside it: at most 500 characters, and an empty note removes it
- `ports` (List of Number) The ports it admits, at most ten; `[443]` when omitted, or the destination's own port with
`from_destination`.
- `repository_ids` (List of String) The repositories whose workloads it applies to, at most 100; every repository when empty.
- `services` (List of String) The services it applies to; every service when empty, or the destination's own service with
`from_destination`.
- `value` (String) The destination: `api.stripe.com` for a host, `*.acme.example` for a domain, `203.0.113.7`
or `203.0.113.0/24` for an address. Required unless `from_destination` is sent.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was written.
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `from_destination_id` (String) A destination an organization's code reached, counted per service, kind, port and decision
- `last_admitted_at` (String) When it last admitted a connection, in the last 90 days.
- `rule_id` (String) An outbound rule: one destination an organization's code may reach
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed.
- `warnings` (Attributes List) What it allows that is easy to miss. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--warnings))

<a id="nestedatt--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor, and empty on a redacted one and on an outside author.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor and on an outside author (`imported`).
- `imported` (Attributes) An author who wrote on another host — a work item, a merge request, a comment, a release an import
brought — and whom nobody here is linked to yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by--imported))
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--created_by--imported"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by.imported`

Read-Only:

- `identity_id` (String) The outside author's id among the organization's imported identities.
- `login` (String) Their login on that host.
- `name` (String) Their name on that host, when it gave one.
- `profile_url` (String) Their profile's address on that host, when it gave one.
- `source_host` (String) The host they wrote on, such as `github.com`.



<a id="nestedatt--warnings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `warnings`

Read-Only:

- `code` (String) What a rule's warning is about.
- `message` (String) The warning, in plain words.
- `suffix` (String) The shared-hosting suffix the rule's name falls under.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and rule_id, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_group_outbound_rule.example "<group_id>/<rule_id>"
```
